summary:
Phase 14B + 14C tested end-to-end. Created /app/backend/tests/test_phase14b_admin_panel.py (39 tests, 33 PASS / 6 FAIL = 84.6%). All 8 new modules in /admin/v2/* (Support Desk, Usage Analytics, System Health, Marketing CRM, Notifications, Audit, Settings, Internal Users + RBAC matrix) work end-to-end including SLA calculation (urgent=2h verified), ticket reply→first_response_at→Resolved flow, incident create/resolve, broadcast→feed delivery to clinic_owner, settings PUT founder-only (sales_manager 403 verified), internal user invite + role validation. Frontend smoke (founder login): /admin/dashboard reached, all 8 new pages (/admin/support, /usage, /system, /marketing, /notifications, /audit, /settings, /users) render with ZERO console errors, sidebar shows 4 groups (Core/Growth/Ops/Governance) with all 15 nav items, FOUNDER role badge correct. Role-based redirects: sales_manager → /admin/dashboard, frontdesk → /frontdesk — both correct.

The 6 backend failures all share ONE root cause: the LEGACY /app/backend/routers/admin_panel.py (Phase 14A) still uses `ADMIN_ROLES = ('founder', 'super_admin')` via require_roles for every endpoint. The new Phase 14C ROLE_PERMISSIONS matrix in admin_panel_b.py is NOT honored by these older routes. So sales_manager cannot read /admin/v2/leads, finance_manager cannot read /admin/v2/revenue or /admin/v2/subscriptions/plans, product_ops cannot write /admin/v2/feature-flags, read_only cannot read /admin/v2/dashboard or /admin/v2/tenants — directly contradicting the review_request RBAC promises.

critical.issue: Legacy admin_panel.py routes use ADMIN_ROLES=('founder','super_admin') only; the new ROLE_PERMISSIONS matrix in admin_panel_b.py is ignored. Result: sales_manager (403 on /leads), finance_manager (403 on /revenue + /subscriptions/plans), product_ops (403 on PUT /feature-flags), read_only (403 on /dashboard + /tenants) — all break the documented RBAC contract from review_request. Fix: replace require_roles(*ADMIN_ROLES) with require_permission('<resource>:read|write') in admin_panel.py, OR have require_roles consult ROLE_PERMISSIONS as a fallback.

minor.issue: Pydantic validation error returns 422 (default) for invalid category before the handler's HTTPException(400) check is reached when other fields are also invalid. Cosmetic — handler does emit 400 for bad category when other fields valid.
email/sms/whatsapp gateways always show status='mocked' (expected, MOCKED). Document for UI badge styling.
leads_generated joins on waitlist_signups.source via case-insensitive regex; if a campaign source contains regex metachars it would mis-match. Use $eq with $regex escape or Python pre-escape.
Heavy N+1 — 6 count_documents per clinic per row. With 6 tenants OK; will scale poorly past ~50 tenants. Consider $facet aggregation.

issues: AVG RESPONSE shows '0h' when there are no replies yet — should show '—' or 'N/A' to differentiate from actual zero.

action_items: CRITICAL: Refactor /app/backend/routers/admin_panel.py — replace `require_roles(*ADMIN_ROLES)` on dashboard/tenants/leads/revenue/subscriptions/feature-flags routes with `require_permission('<resource>:<verb>')` using the matrix from admin_panel_b.py. This single change unblocks all 5 internal roles. Alternatively, modify auth.require_roles to fall through to ROLE_PERMISSIONS when role not in the explicit list.
Optional: when role denies, return 403 with body={'detail': 'Role X lacks permission Y'} for consistency with admin_panel_b (it currently returns 'Requires one of: (...)').
Optional: cosmetic — show '—' instead of '0h' on empty avg_response_hrs / avg_resolution_hrs.
critical_code_review_comments: ROLE_PERMISSIONS matrix is well-designed (read/write verbs + wildcards) but only enforced on Phase 14B/C endpoints. Phase 14A endpoints (admin_panel.py) bypass it entirely — the 5 new internal roles are effectively useless on legacy modules. This is the highest-impact bug in this PR.
admin_panel_b.has_permission() correctly handles wildcards ('*', '*:read', '*:write'). Founder + super_admin bypass at top of require_permission — clean.
Tickets create/update + SLA timer (2/8/24/72h) implemented per spec. first_response_at and resolved_at correctly set conditionally. Thread append uses $push with $each — correct.
Settings PUT correctly gates founder/super_admin only with explicit role check (not require_permission) — good defensive choice.
Notifications target_count is correctly derived from clinics matching the audience filter; in-app feed query uses $or with audience='all' fallback — works for clinic_owners.

Notification audience='tier' uppercases the filter before matching subscription_tier — but if filter is None it sets q to empty-string match (bug: empty audience_filter on 'tier' will match no clinics silently rather than 400). Add validation.
Internal user invite uses bcrypt via auth.hash_password — good. Email lowercased before existence check.
Marketing CAC = budget / converted; division-by-zero guarded. Source matching is case-insensitive regex but unsafe with regex metacharacters in source strings.
Audit filtered viewer uses regex on actor/action/target — same regex injection risk; for an internal admin tool acceptable.
System health gateway statuses default to 'mocked' string when collection empty — clean MOCKED indicator; UI must display badge accordingly.
Incident resolve correctly fails 404 when already-resolved (uses {resolved_at: None} filter).

rca of the issue:
RCA — 6 RBAC test failures: /app/backend/routers/admin_panel.py:51 declares `ADMIN_ROLES = ('founder', 'super_admin')` and every endpoint in that file uses `require_roles(*ADMIN_ROLES)` (lines 74, 238, 289, 339, 359, 371, 383, 439, 474, 499, 545, 570, 631, 653, 704, 730, 755). When the Phase 14C ROLE_PERMISSIONS matrix was added in admin_panel_b.py, the legacy routes were not migrated. So a sales_manager JWT hitting GET /admin/v2/leads gets 403 'Requires one of: (founder, super_admin)' before any matrix check happens. Reproduction: login as sales@audinexa.com → curl GET /api/admin/v2/leads → 403. Mitigation (one of):
  (A) Replace require_roles in admin_panel.py with require_permission('<resource>:<verb>') from admin_panel_b — preferred.
  (B) Make auth.require_roles consult ROLE_PERMISSIONS when the user's role isn't in the explicit list (broader change, lower risk to existing routes).
  (C) Expand ADMIN_ROLES per endpoint (error-prone, defeats the purpose of the matrix).
